text: CUNY Fast App – The City University of New York Skip to Content Skip to Navigation Instructions on the CUNY Fast App Application Process for New York City Public High School (NYCPS) Students NYCPS students can now fill out and submit a streamlined, simplified version of the CUNY application that uses the information we are able to receive from NYCPS using their OSIS number to reduce the number of steps in completing their application. Jump to: Tutorial Instructions FAQs Tutorial Please watch this tutorial to give you an overview of the Fast App application process. Instructions 1. Identity Confirmation Input your 9 digit OSIS number. Input your date of birth, first, and last name. (Make sure to follow the date convention, and use the name attached to your OSIS number) Verify your identity by correctly answering the multiple choice security question 2. Application Dashboard/Your Profile Review the information already provided and update it if necessary. Ensure your answers to the prompts are as accurate as possible. Click on your Home Address to update it if necessary Indicate if your legal name is different from the name listed on your school record or if you’ve had any former names 3. Personal Details Enter your country of citizenship. If your country of citizenship is the United States, provide your country of birth. If your country of citizenship is outside the United States, provide your immigration status, visa or permit type, the date issued, expiration date, and country of birth Indicate if you have an SSN and enter it if applicable Indicate your military status Respond to the prompts regarding your ethnicity 4. Education History 5. College and Major Choose the term you are applying for Fall: August – December Spring: January – Ma Select “Add a college choice” Choose a college from the dropdown menu and click “Search” Scroll through the listed options and choose your intended major Repeat to choose up to 6 different You can only choose one major per college, you can not apply to the same college for two different programs. 6. Financial Aid Indicate your living arrangements for the upcoming academic year Indicate your interest in Federal Work-Study 7. Fee Payment Choose between “Pay Now”, “Pay Later”, or “I have a CUNY Issued fee waiver” (if you have been issued a CUNY fee waiver) Please see your high school college counselor to request a fee waiver. If you are waiting to receive one, select “Pay Later”. Click “Make a Payment and Submit Application” Review the Applicant Certification Statement and ensure that the information you have input is as accurate and up to date as possible. Check the box to certify that the information you have provided is accurate. Click “Continue”, and allow the page to process your application, this can take a few moments. 8. Nelnet If you have selected “Pay Now”, you will be redirected to Nelnet, our secure payment partner. If this page does not show up, ensure that your browser’s pop-up blocker is disabled, or give your browser permission for the page to “allow pop-ups”. Click “Next-Payment Method” Select a payment method and input your payment information Once your payment is confirmed, click “OK” Congratulations, you have successfully submitted your CUNY application! You will be able to view a summary of your application by clicking “View/Print Summary” and find your CUNYfirst ID number under the “Personal Information” section. Apply Here Click Here to Apply FAQs What is the FastApp? The Fast App is a streamlined college application for New York City Public School (NYCPS) students who are applying to CUNY as first-time Freshmen. It draws upon relevant information from NYCPS transcripts to pre-fill the CUNY application form, thereby expediting the application submission process. Who can use the Fast App? The Fast App is available to freshman applicants currently attending New York City Public Schools. It is not available to applicants from non-NYCPS schools, transfer or Macaulay Honors College applicants. What semesters are available for Fast App? The Fast App will first be available for the Spring 2026 semester. What information is pre-filled in the Fast App? Fast App auto-populates the following from NYCPS data: Home Address and Phone Number Name (as it appears on the NYCPS transcript) Date of Birth NYCPS School, Class Year What are all the sections on Fast App? The Fast App will present applicants with the sections requiring applicants to review/provide information for following elements to complete their application. Additionally, the Fast App will automatically populate applicant details using NYCPS data available within CUNYfirst, streamlining the application process. Your Profile (Name, Contact Info) Citizenship & Background Education College Choice(s) Financial Aid Ǫuestions Application Fee Payment Where do I find the link for the Fast App application? The link can be found on the Apply Now page, here . How does the application fee work? Fast App applicants can pay by debit card, eCheck, or have their college counselor request a fee waiver through the CUNY Counselor Portal. Students are able to return to pay their application after submitting the application, however applications will not be reviewed until the application fee is paid or waived. How can applicants track their application? Once submitted, applicants can use Admissions Self Service feature on CUNYfirst to view their application status: missing checklist items, document submissions with dates, status of evaluation and recommendations. etc. What about accessibility and accommodation? The Fast App is compliant with ADA, Section 504, and NYS Accessibility Policies. CUNY ensures all materials and interactions are accessible, with additional support through each campus Disability Services Office. Is the Fast App mobile friendly? Yes, it is fully usable on smartphones, tablets, and desktops. How long does it take to complete Fast App? Compared to the standard 17-22 minute online application, Fast App takes less time due to pre-filled data and fewer steps. On average, applicants can complete the FastApp in 5-10 minutes. Is the application legally binding upon submission? Yes. Applicants must acknowledge a legal statement before submission. How secure is the application? Fast App security includes public access authentication without account creation, role- based data access via PeopleSoft Student Administration C Contributor Relations (SACR) security roles and alignment with CUNY’s digital asset security policies. What if I already submitted the standard CUNY application or the Macaulay Honors application—can I still use Fast App? No. Applicants should submit only one application per admissions cycle. If you are interested in Macaulay Honors, you must submit the Macaulay application only and should not use the Fast App or the standard CUNY application. Will the Fast App ask for recommendation letters or personal statements? No. Fast App does not require personal statements or letters of recommendation. However, specific colleges or programs may request additional materials after submission. Authentication G Access How is data authenticated in the Fast App? The application will utilize applicant transcript data provided by NYCPS for data matching, authorization, and authentication. How do I access the Fast App? To access the Fast App, students must authenticate using: OSIS number (NYCPS 9-digit Unique ID) Date of Birth (MM/DD/YYYY) First and Last Name Verifying Institution and other transcript information (if needed) The system cross-checks these with NYCPS records and follows up with verification questions (randomly selected) to further confirm identity. What happens if I fail the verification process? If verification fails: The OSIS ID is locked The applicant is redirected to the standard Online Application Can I retrieve applicant’s access if they are locked out? Applicants should speak to their guidance counselors before using the Fast App to confirm their name spelling and DOB that are currently on file with NYCPS. Applicants who are unable to authenticate their identity using the Fast App will still have the ability to apply using the standard Freshman or Macaulay applications. Can I save and return to the Fast App? Yes. The Fast App sends a one-time access code to the applicant’s email address so that returning applicants can complete their initiated applications. Is Name Change available on the Fast App? To update a legal name or add a former name not shown on NYCPS transcripts, applicants should use the indicators on the ‘Your Profile’ page of the Fast App. Following application submission, they will be granted access to the CUNYfirst system where they can use self-service tools to make those changes. Can an applicant update their phone number? Yes. Applicants will have the opportunity to provide both a home and cell phone number. Can an applicant update their email address? Yes. Can home addresses be updated in the Fast App? Yes. Would applicants still receive an application summary in the Fast App? Yes, it will be available after submission. Can applicants indicate prior attendance at a prior non-NYCPS high school or attendance at a non-CUNY college? Yes. Applicants who attended other high schools that are not listed on their ‘Education’ page, or who attended a college before graduating from high school, can report that attendance by activating an indicator on the ‘Education’ page, as needed to complete their education history. How are Fee Waivers handled? The application fee is automatically waived for NYCPS applicants who apply during the free application period. NYCPS applicants are strongly encouraged to apply during that time. The FastApp fee page also accepts fee waiver codes. In addition, NYCPS counselors may utilize the Counselor Portal to submit fee waivers for individual applicants. How are supporting documents handled? Once the application is submitted and access to the CUNYfirst system is granted, the applicant can use the self-service tool to upload supporting materials other than their application file. NYCPS counselors may upload materials and other official records to their students’ applications using the Counselor Portal. After submitting their application, the student will receive an email notice to claim their CUNYfirst account and gain access to their Student Services Center.

Will the Fast App ask for recommendation letters or personal statements? No. Fast App does not require personal statements or letters of recommendation. However, specific colleges or programs may request additional materials after submission. Authentication G Access How is data authenticated in the Fast App? The application will utilize applicant transcript data provided by NYCPS for data matching, authorization, and authentication. How do I access the Fast App? What happens if I fail the verification process? If verification fails: The OSIS ID is locked The applicant is redirected to the standard Online Application Can I retrieve applicant’s access if they are locked out? Applicants should speak to their guidance counselors before using the Fast App to confirm their name spelling and DOB that are currently on file with NYCPS. Once the application is submitted and access to the CUNYfirst system is granted, the applicant can use the self-service tool to upload supporting materials other than their application file. NYCPS counselors may upload materials and other official records to their students’ applications using the Counselor Portal.
